description: TeajiA tea tasting taxonomy. Structured around somatic awareness: sensation first, naming last. Hints appear only on terms where the word alone is not enough.

categories.name: Sensation
categories.description: What your mouth reports. Temperature, weight, texture.

groups.label: Weight
groups.hint: How much space does the tea take up in your mouth? Like water, or like broth?

groups.label: Texture
groups.hint: How does it move? Does it slide, grip, coat, or prickle?

terms.label: Silky
terms.hint: The tea slides across your tongue with no resistance.

terms.label: Smooth
terms.hint: Even and gentle, nothing catches. Easy to drink.

terms.label: Velvety
terms.hint: Soft and plush, a little more weight than silky.

terms.label: Oily
terms.hint: Coats your mouth, feels rich. Almost buttery.

terms.label: Taut
terms.hint: Crisp structure, a little tension. Like biting into a fresh apple.

terms.label: Astringent
terms.hint: Drying, puckering. The same feeling as strong black tea or unripe fruit.

categories.name: Movement
categories.description: What happens as you swallow. Follow the tea down.

groups.label: Throat
groups.hint: Follow the tea past your tongue. Does your throat feel open, narrow, coated?

terms.label: Opens
terms.hint: Your throat feels wider, more relaxed after swallowing. The tea opens a path.

terms.label: Deep reach
terms.hint: You feel the tea not just in your mouth but deep in your throat. It travels.

terms.label: Coats
terms.hint: A layer stays behind on your tongue and throat after swallowing.

terms.label: Mouth waters
terms.hint: Your mouth produces saliva in response. The tea makes you want more.

groups.label: Duration
groups.hint: After swallowing, is the sensation already gone? Or still here?

terms.label: Lingering
terms.hint: The taste stays and stays. Minutes later, you can still find it.

groups.label: Character
groups.hint: Wait a few seconds after swallowing. Is something coming back?

terms.label: Hui gan
terms.hint: Wait 10 seconds. A sweetness rising in the back of your throat that was not there before. The most prized quality in Chinese tea.

terms.label: Sweet return
terms.hint: Similar to hui gan. A gentle sweetness that appears after the initial taste fades.

terms.label: Clean
terms.hint: After swallowing, the taste disappears completely. No residue, no aftertaste hanging around.

terms.label: Dry
terms.hint: A dryness settles in after swallowing. Your mouth feels like it needs water.

terms.label: Cooling
terms.hint: A coolness appears in your throat after swallowing, like menthol but gentler.

terms.label: Warming
terms.hint: Warmth spreads from your throat after swallowing. A slow, pleasant heat.

categories.name: Feeling
categories.description: What the tea does to your state. Beyond flavor, into presence.

groups.label: Settling
groups.hint: Did your breathing change? Do you feel more still than before you drank?

terms.label: Calming
terms.hint: The busy mind slows down. Breathing gets easier.

terms.label: Grounding
terms.hint: Notice your feet and your seat. You feel more here, more settled.

terms.label: Centering
terms.hint: Scattered energy draws inward. You feel collected, gathered.

groups.label: Lifting
groups.hint: Do you feel more awake? Is your mind sharper or brighter?

terms.label: Energizing
terms.hint: Brightness without jitteriness. You want to move.

terms.label: Uplifting
terms.hint: Your mood lifts. Things feel lighter than before.

terms.label: Focusing
terms.hint: Thoughts sharpen. One thing at a time.

terms.label: Clarifying
terms.hint: Mental fog lifts. Things feel simpler.

groups.label: Body
groups.hint: Scan from your throat to your belly. Any warmth spreading? Any tightness letting go?

terms.label: Warming
terms.hint: Warmth spreading through your chest or belly. Not from the temperature, from the tea itself.

terms.label: Cooling
terms.hint: A coolness moving through you. Refreshing, opening.

terms.label: Chest opens
terms.hint: A physical warmth or expansion in the chest. Like taking a deep breath became easier.

terms.label: Tension releases
terms.hint: Shoulders drop, jaw unclenches. You did not know you were holding.

groups.label: Mind
groups.hint: Where is your mind right now? Quiet? Busy? Somewhere in between?

terms.label: Present
terms.hint: You are here. Not thinking about later or before. Just now.

terms.label: Contemplative
terms.hint: Thoughts are moving slowly and with weight. Reflective, not rushed.

terms.label: Expansive
terms.hint: Your sense of space widens. Things feel open, spacious.

terms.label: Restless
terms.hint: Hard to settle. The tea stirred something up rather than calming it down.

categories.name: Flavor
categories.description: What you taste. Pick the family first, then get specific if you want.

groups.label: Floral
groups.hint: Anything fragrant or perfumed? Like passing a garden.

terms.label: Osmanthus
terms.hint: A sweet, apricot-like fragrance. Common in oolong and some white teas.

groups.label: Sweet
groups.hint: Not added sweetness. Does the tea itself carry any sweetness?

terms.label: Cream
terms.hint: A dairy-like richness. Common in high-mountain oolongs and some white teas.

groups.label: Fruity
groups.hint: Bright, juicy, ripe? Fresh fruit or dried fruit?

terms.label: Stone fruit
terms.hint: Peach, plum, apricot territory. A broad family if you are not sure which one.

terms.label: Tropical
terms.hint: Mango, passionfruit, pineapple territory. Lush and exotic.

groups.label: Nutty & grain
groups.hint: Warm and toasted? Like roasted nuts or fresh bread.

groups.label: Roasted & warm
groups.hint: Deep warmth from fire. Cocoa, toast, smoke.

groups.label: Spice
groups.hint: Warm spice notes. Think kitchen spice rack, not chili heat.

terms.label: Cinnamon
terms.hint: Fundamental to Wuyi yancha. Rou gui literally means cinnamon.

groups.label: Woody
groups.hint: Forest notes. Bark, sap, temple incense.

terms.label: Camphor
terms.hint: A cooling, medicinal wood note. Common in aged puerh and some aged oolongs.

terms.label: Resinous
terms.hint: Sticky, sappy. Like tree resin or amber.

groups.label: Mineral
groups.hint: Stone and rock. Like the smell after rain on pavement.

groups.label: Fresh & vegetal
groups.hint: Green and alive. Cut grass, steamed vegetables, the garden.

groups.label: Taste & character
groups.hint: Fundamental tastes and qualities beyond flavor. Does it bite, deepen, or pucker?

terms.label: Bitter
terms.hint: Not a flaw in Chinese tea. Bitterness that transforms into sweetness is highly prized.

terms.label: Sour
terms.hint: A tangy, tart edge. Common in young sheng puerh and some oolongs.

terms.label: Umami
terms.hint: A deep, brothy savoriness. Like the richness in seaweed or aged cheese.

terms.label: Aged
terms.hint: The taste of time. A depth and complexity that only comes from years of storage.

terms.label: Fermented
terms.hint: Distinct from aged. The result of microbial transformation, as in shou puerh or liu bao.

categories.name: Appearance
categories.description: What you see in the cup.

categories.name: Brewing suggestion
categories.description: A nudge, not a recipe. How to approach this tea.

groups.label: Session arc
groups.hint: How does the tea change across steeps?

terms.label: Opens slowly
terms.hint: The tea holds back at first, then reveals itself over several steeps.

terms.label: Peaks mid-session
terms.hint: The best steeps come in the middle, not the beginning.

terms.label: Consistent
terms.hint: The tea stays steady from steep to steep. Reliable, no big surprises.

terms.label: Fades gracefully
terms.hint: As the tea thins, it remains pleasant. A gentle ending, not an abrupt drop.
